# Third-Party Source Checkouts

`agent-runtime/` is a Git submodule pinned to the standalone Rust agent runtime
repository. Update runtime crates, schemas, fixtures, CLI, and evals in that
repository first, then advance this submodule pointer in NaviWealth.

`nsh-platform-android/` vendors the Apache-2.0 crates.io 0.4.0 release from
https://github.com/longbridge/nsh. The local patches expose the absolute app
data root to native Rust components and add Storage Access Framework exchange
for encrypted backups. The document bridge uses a retained Android fragment
for system picker results and copies bytes through `ContentResolver`; Rust
never treats a `content://` URI as a filesystem path. No broad storage
permission is needed.

Root keyboard dismissal also uses the focused input's own window token, so
inputs inside native dialogs can dismiss the IME and release focus correctly.

`.cargo/config.toml` applies the Rust patch to both Cargo workspaces (including
the runner generated by nsh). Build Android with `tool/build-client-android.sh`:
it compiles the vendored Java with javac/D8, packages the Rust runtime, replaces
the prebuilt DEX in the APK, then aligns and signs the final artifact. Plain
`nsh package` uses the upstream prebuilt Java and will not include document
exchange; the app detects that missing capability and reports it explicitly.
The wrapper accepts `--abi x86_64` for emulator builds. SDK platform 35,
build-tools 35+, JDK 17+, nsh 0.4.0 and an NDK configured for Cargo are required.
A supplied `NAVIWEALTH_ANDROID_KEYSTORE`, `NAVIWEALTH_ANDROID_KEY_ALIAS` and
`NSH_KEYSTORE_PASSWORD` select a signing key; the default is a local debug key
under the gitignored `apps/client/.nsh/signing/` directory.

Keep these narrow patches until upstream provides native app paths and mobile
document exchange. Do not edit generated files in `apps/client/.nsh/`.
